projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 20–23 device count paired with zero camera motion suggests either guests are visiting, the family is gathered in a single room, or neighbor Wi-Fi is bleeding into the network; verifying camera functionality and checking for expected visitors would clarify the situation.

The sustained connection of 20–23 mobile devices to the home network, paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon, strongly suggests either unreported guests are present (possibly in a camera-blind zone) or the presence system is miscounting IoT devices as phones. Steve should verify network activity and camera status to rule out unauthorized access or sensor misconfiguration.

The sustained 21–24 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Monday afternoon strongly indicates the home is unoccupied, with the elevated count likely driven by background IoT devices rather than occupants; verify if guests are expected or if the children returned early.

The sustained 20–23 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates a presence detection glitch or stale network connections rather than actual occupancy, especially since the school-age children would typically be out.

The sustained 20–22 device count paired with zero camera motion over four hours on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates the house is unoccupied, with the high device count driven by stationary smart home/IoT equipment rather than human presence. This clarifies that presence sensors are counting networked appliances, preventing false occupancy alerts.

The sustained 20–22 device count paired with zero camera motion on a Monday afternoon strongly indicates the home is unoccupied and the presence detection is likely miscounting IoT devices, cached connections, or experiencing a network glitch. This matters because it confirms a false-positive occupancy state that could skew automation logic or reporting.

The sustained 20–24 device count paired with zero camera motion over four hours on a Monday morning indicates an unreported gathering or network misconfiguration, as normal family activity would typically trigger cameras or show a lower device count.

The active device count (20-24) significantly exceeds the household size, and its steady decline to 20 over 90 minutes—combined with zero camera motion on a Monday morning—suggests a group of visitors is dispersing or a smart home network is cycling IoT devices. A quick check is warranted to rule out lingering guests or network misreporting.

The combination of 20-24 reported mobile devices and zero camera activity on a Monday morning suggests the presence sensor is likely counting IoT/smart home devices as phones, or the house is unoccupied with devices still connected to Wi-Fi. Confirming the home is empty or adjusting the presence filter would prevent false occupancy assumptions for automations.

The network consistently reports 20-25 active mobile devices, significantly exceeding the expected count for a four-person household and two dogs. This likely indicates numerous smart home/IoT devices are being misclassified as mobile, but worth verifying to rule out unlogged guests or unauthorized connections.
